title: Courier profile - paas_driver
lede: Not hand-drawn. Every frame below is the actual route paas_driver composes for the courier profile - delivery_sdk's ProfilePage shell hosting base_sdk's GenericProfilePage, with delivery_sdk's own driver sections registered into it - rendered headlessly to PNG by test/render/render_screen_test.dart at 390 logical px / dpr 3, with the numbered points placed automatically from each widget's measured rect. Data is the SDKs' own demo fixtures (IS_DEMO=true), never a live backend.

notes.kicker: note - how these renders were produced
body: A widget test in this repo; zero app code touched. It pumps the real ProfilePage that delivery_sdk installs into lib/presentation/pages/profile/, which is now a route shell: it registers delivery_sdk's driver sections and then hosts base_sdk's GenericProfilePage inside a PlaneHost, with the floating back pill in the route Stack above it. The harness wraps that page exactly as lib/presentation/app_widget.dart wraps every screen (ProviderScope, ScreenUtilInit at the app's 375x812 compact design size, and the app's own theme, darkTheme and themeMode arguments copied verbatim), renders it at 390 logical px (dpr 3) at the page's full content height, and captures the RepaintBoundary to PNG.

The data is the SDKs' own demo data, not fixtures written for this page. The test runs with --dart-define=IS_DEMO=true and calls the same DI registrations lib/main.dart's generated blocks make, so DriverDeliveryDependencies installs DemoCourierRepository, DriverRevenueDependencies installs DemoCourierStatisticsRepository and AuthSdkDependencies installs MockAuthRepository - the same demo fixtures a demo build of the driver app serves. Everything on the frames is the app's own computation over that data: the courier's identity, the R480.00 last profit and the 128 delivered orders all come back from the demo repositories.

Real, not simulated: Inter is the genuine face Google serves, committed beside the test and handed to google_fonts through its own test seam, which verifies each file's length and SHA-256 before registering it. The icon fonts (MaterialIcons, Remix) are registered from the app's own FontManifest. AppStyle's light/dark tokens are resolved by the app's own AppNotifier through the real setBrightness seam. Layout, spacing, typography, colour, row order and visibility gates are all the shipped code path.

Every finder is arity-checked before the frame is measured (verifyFinders in the harness): each numbered element must resolve to exactly one widget, the row list to exactly nine, and the anonymous header to none. A page that changes underneath the harness fails the test rather than quietly dropping or duplicating a numbered point.

notes.kicker: exception - the session the demo mode cannot supply
body: Demo mode covers repositories; it does not hand a widget test a SESSION. The identity card reads LocalStorage.getUser(), which auth_sdk writes in _establishSession when a courier signs in, and a widget test never walks that journey.

So the harness signs in the way the app does (marker 3/8): through the REAL AuthRepositoryFacade.login - which demo mode has already made MockAuthRepository - as driver@demo.rokct.ai, maps the account with auth_sdk's own sessionProfileOf, and persists it through the app's own LocalStorage API. Every value on the identity card is the SDK's demo account, not a number typed in here.

The earnings figures are filled by the same call the courier's own journey makes: home_page.dart's initState fires fetchProfileStatistics before profile is ever reached, so the harness fires it too, against revenue_sdk's demo statistics repository. Reached cold, those figures render zeroes - which is itself worth knowing.

notes.kicker: declared - the radio a headless runner does not have
body: These frames are captured ONLINE, and that is a deliberate declaration rather than a side effect. Every backend read on this page passes AppConnectivity.connectivity(), which is connectivity_plus' checkConnectivity() over a platform channel. A widget test has no such plugin, and answering the channel with null is not neutral: connectivity_plus parses null as an empty transport list - a handset with no radio at all - so the profile host's own fetchUser took its offline branch and raised the 'No internet connection / Close' SnackBar across the bottom of both frames.

So the harness answers that one call the way a connected handset answers it (['wifi'], marker in _mockAbsentPlugins) and captures the screen a courier with a working connection actually sees. Nothing else is faked: no HTTP is served, no fixture is written, and every repository behind that check is still the SDK's own demo implementation - the page is filled by unchanged app logic over demo data, which is exactly why the wallet now shows the demo account's real balance. base_sdk's profile footer already takes the same position for the same reason: its Online dot reads connected on a demo build instead of drawing a red Offline for a backend the build was never meant to have.

The harness asserts the outcome, it does not just hope for it: verifyFinders fails the run if any SnackBar is on the frame. An offline, maintenance or error state must never reach the guided tour, the user guide or the deck, and a render that quietly burns one in is worse than no render.

notes.kicker: found by rendering (a drawing could not have caught these)
items: Balance reads R793.00 because the profile fetch runs: base_sdk's GenericProfilePage fires profileProvider.fetchUser on its first frame, users_sdk's demo MockUserRepository answers it, and the account's wallet lands on the header. It read R0.00 for as long as the capture was offline - the login contract's user carries no wallet (sessionProfileOf leaves the profile-only fields to that fetch), and an offline fetch never made it. The zero was the headless runner showing, not the app.

The row labels are humanized translation-key fallbacks, not served strings: no backend answers headlessly, so AppHelpers.humanizeTrKey is what a reviewer is reading ('Profile settings', 'Order history'). That is also exactly what a first-run demo build shows before the translations fetch lands.

'Delete account' is absent by design: the row sits behind a demo gate, and the render runs in demo mode - the gate is the shipped code path, not a harness omission. The harness asserts its absence rather than assuming it.

The back pill is viewport-anchored rather than content-anchored - it floats in the route Stack, above the page - so it carries no chip: numbering it would pin the frame height to the harness probe height rather than the page's own content height. It is still product UI, and the harness asserts it is there.

Two elements rendered as solid white blocks until the harness registered the generic font families they ask for. The Back pill sits above the page with no Material ancestor, so its bare TextStyle inherits WidgetsApp's fallback style, whose family is 'monospace'; and the demo avatar is an inline SVG whose text asks for 'Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif', which vector_graphics_compiler passes to the engine whole, as one family name. A device resolves both to real system faces; a headless test engine has neither registered and falls through to the Ahem block font. Not a missing Inter weight - all four committed weights were already loading.
The gap between 'Languages' and the buttons is the page's own nav clearance, not padding.

notes.kicker: why the profile and not the home
body: The courier home is this shell's landing screen, but it is a full-bleed GoogleMap platform view plus Geolocator, FirebaseMessaging and WorkManager. Headless, the map surface never fetches a tile and renders as a blank grey grid, so the frame would be a picture of nothing.

The profile is the next-densest driver-owned surface - identity card, courier stats, and the whole settings register - and it renders entirely from base_sdk's, delivery_sdk's and revenue_sdk's demo repositories. Home is worth covering once someone decides what a map surface should look like in a review frame.
